newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - SEPT 17.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - SEPT 17.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs still believes that the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty was the reachable best solution.
- Hungarian Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman promised to set the higher energy prices by the end of November.
- Hungary will soon continue trials on the 1956 squad shootings. The trials will be based on international laws.

- According to former Foreign Minister, now opposition politician Geza Jeszenszky, the signing of the Romanian-Hungarian basic treaty was urgent for two reasons. One is that Prime Minister Gyula Horn and his government wants to support at the Romanian elections those Romanian forces which committed everything in the past six years to hinder the real approach between Hungarians and Romanians. The other reason was the western pressure.

- Hungary is considering more than 800 requests for a 1956 award which is accompanied with a supplementary pension. More than 10,000 people submitted such request. Only those may be awarded who fighted with guns during the uprising or did outstanding job in one of the revolutionary organisations.
